item.title: Polarity‐Directed Assembly of in‐Plane Oriented Covalent Organic Framework Films on Substrates
item.description:
High-quality in-plane oriented COF films have been synthesized by polarity-directed solution assembly strategy. By constructing a heterojunction with perovskite, it can passivate the buried defects of the perovskite film at the interface by virtue of its ordered pore structure and a large number of coordination sites. When used as active layers, PeLED devices exhibit high performance.


ABSTRACT

Two-dimensional (2D) covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) are promising crystalline porous materials for optoelectronic applications; however, controlled growth of COF thin films on substrates remains a significant challenge. Here, we develop a polarity-directed solution assembly strategy for the fabrication of 2D COF thin films on various substrates. This approach leverages polarity-driven solvent–molecule interactions to regulate precursor assembly and oriented polymerization, successfully yielding in-plane oriented COF films with controllable thickness, smooth surface morphology, and abundant nitrogen active sites. When these films are used as templates for perovskite growth, the resulting heterojunction interfaces effectively passivate buried interfacial defects and suppress non-radiative recombination. Integrated into light-emitting diodes (LED), the devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 30.88%, a peak luminance of 1.7 × 105 cd/m2, and an operational half-lifetime (T50) of 12.74 h at an initial luminance of 9206 cd/m2 (equivalent to >6238 h at 100 cd/m2), surpassing most previously reported counterparts. This work opens a new molecular regulation avenue toward the preparation of highly oriented COF films for versatile optoelectronic applications.

item.title: Continuous Tuning of Magnetic Bistability via Consecutive Desolvation and Decoupled Structural Phase Transition
item.description:
Through combined structural, magnetic, and thermal analyses of intermediates isolated during SCSC desolvation, this work decouples desolvation from the subsequent thermally induced structural phase transition, enabling continuous modulation of SCO properties in an FeIII complex. A quantitative linear correlation between the phase transition extent and the high-spin population was established, offering a new strategy for fine-tuning magnetic bistability.


ABSTRACT

Achieving precise and continuous modulation of magnetic bistability remains a key challenge in advancing the practical utility of molecular magnetic materials. Herein, we exploit the consecutive desolvation and the following decoupled, thermally induced structural phase transition (SPT) to finely regulate the magnetic bistability in a mononuclear FeIII SCO complex. This complex evolves from an abrupt SCO with a transition temperature (T 1/2) of 264 K to a hysteretic two-step transition (T 1/2↓ = 132 K, T 1/2↑ = 155 K, ∆T = 23 K), and finally to a locked high-spin (HS) state, which occurs via single-crystal-to-single-crystal transformations. More importantly, a quantitative linear correlation between the SPT progression and the HS/LS ratio is established by fine-tuning the annealing temperature and duration. This work demonstrates that the consecutive desolvation and decoupled SPT offer a new strategy for the continuous regulation of the key parameters of SCO-based magnetic bistable materials.

item.title: Protein Secondary Structure From Infrared Spectroscopy—Tricks to Use and Traps to Avoid
item.description:
The article critically assesses protein secondary structure analysis by infrared spectroscopy with a focus on the popular approach that fits the amide I band of the protein backbone. The figure shows a fit (blue) to the absorbance spectrum (green) of the sarcoplasmic reticulum Ca2+-ATPase.


ABSTRACT

Secondary structure analysis of proteins is one of the major applications of infrared spectroscopy in the life sciences. It requires high quality spectra and their adequate interpretation. This article aims to guide practitioners in generating and interpreting protein infrared spectra, as well as help readers and reviewers assess the quality of the resulting articles. It addresses common problems and mistakes, simple quality criteria and measures for improved spectrum quality and interpretation. Regarding experimental procedures, the text discusses avoidance of water vapor, effects of air bubbles, reduction of noise, and criteria for judging spectrum quality. The secondary structure analysis section focuses on a particular approach in which the amide I region of the spectrum is represented by fitted component bands. The following aspects of the approach are considered: application of band-narrowing techniques, fitting of spectra, assignment of component bands and the accuracy of secondary structure analysis. The purpose is not to provide a single best practice protocol but to make the reader aware of the implications, limitations, pitfalls, and improvement potentials of the used procedures.

item.title: Dense Metalloporphyrin Arrays Enable Binuclear Cooperativity for Enhanced Electrocatalytic Oxygen Reduction
item.description:
A gallium–pyrazolate framework (Ga-TPzP) with densely packed Co-porphyrin arrays features two parallel metalloporphyrin units at an optimal distance of 6.53 Å creating confined nanoreactors, enabling strong hydrogen bonds between coordinated H2O and adsorbed O2 on adjacent Co(II) centers. This unique configuration facilitates O2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, thereby lowering kinetic barrier and significantly enhancing ORR performance.


ABSTRACT

The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is central to clean energy technologies like fuel cells and metal-air batteries, yet its efficiency relies on costly platinum catalysts. In nature, cytochrome c oxidase achieves efficient ORR at a heme iron-copper binuclear center, where hydrogen bonding stabilizes key intermediates. Here, by mimicking this concept, we constructed a gallium–pyrazolate framework (Ga-TPzP) with densely packed Co(II)-porphyrin arrays. The precise arrangement of these sites at an optimal distance of 6.53 Å creates confined nanoreactors, enabling strong hydrogen bonds between coordinated H2O and adsorbed O2 on two adjacent Co(II) centers. This unique binuclear cooperativity facilitates O2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, thereby lowering the kinetic barrier and significantly enhancing the ORR performance. As a cathode in a zinc-air battery, Ga-TPzP(Co) achieves a peak power density of 185 mW cm− 2 and can operate steadily for 150 h at 10 mA cm−2, representing one of the best performance among all reported MOF-based catalysts for this application.

item.title: Evolution of Color in Highly Transparent Emulsions
item.description:
A highly stable, optically transparent liquid–liquid emulsion exhibits brilliant structural colors. By engineering refractive index dispersion matching, dynamic color shifts across the full visible spectrum are achieved within 25°C–43°C window. This designing principle can be extended to a variety of emulsion systems, providing a new platform for optical applications of emulsions.


ABSTRACT

This paper presents highly stable, dynamically tunable and transparent colored emulsions. A typical system is formulated with 1-octadecene droplets (0.5–1.0 µm) dispersed in a water–glycerol (volume ratio of 21:79) continuous phase stabilized by ethylene-1,2-bis(dodecyldimethylammonium bromide). By precisely engineering the refractive index matching between the two phases, the emulsion achieves nearly 100% transmittance at the matching wavelength λ c, exhibiting saturated, wavelength-selective coloration. Owing to the distinct thermo-optic coefficients (dn/dT) of the two phases, the macroscopic color reversibly shifts from blue to purple, purplish-red and orange–yellow ultimately reaching yellow, covering almost the entire visible spectrum between 25°C and 43°C. Composition titration experiments showed the relationship between the macroscopic color shift of the emulsion and the microscopic refractive index matching of the two phases. The scattering efficiency of a single emulsion droplet is calculated based on the van de Hulst approximation. The result reveals that the macroscopic vividness of colors originates from the cumulative scattering effects of a large number of droplets. As water and glycerol can mix in any ratio, this designing principle can not only be successfully applied to other olefins and diverse multi-component oil combinations, exhibiting exceptional formulation adaptability, but also opens up potential applications for optical filters and sensors.

item.title: Biomimetic Reversible Phase Transition in Scandium‐Based Metal Halides for Environment‐Interactive Information Security
item.description:
A biomimetic system based on interconvertible zero-dimensional Cs4ScCl7·H2O and Cs2ScCl5·H2O is developed via a simple “dissolve–dry” method, enabling bidirectional phase transition and reversible color switching. DFT calculations rationalize phase selectivity through kinetic–thermodynamic competition. Sb/lanthanide doping endows stimuli-responsive cyclic switching of STE, downshifting, and upconversion luminescence, empowering zero-error PUF-based anti-counterfeiting and hierarchical dynamic encryption with robust cloning resistance.


ABSTRACT

Inspired by the dynamic adaptive coloration of cephalopods, mimicking their reversible, environment-interactive response behavior is essential for biomimetic material design. The high color purity, multi-wavelength tunability, long luminescence lifetimes, excellent stability, and reversible stimuli-responsive behavior of lanthanide-based emitters render them indispensable in biomimetic camouflage, intelligent sensing, electronic skin, and adaptive optical materials. In this study, we develop a biomimetic system based on zero‑dimensional Cs4ScCl7·H2O and its interconvertible counterpart Cs2ScCl5·H2O via a simple “dissolve–dry” method. Bidirectional phase transitions are achieved by facile alternating ScCl3 and CsCl treatment. Density functional theory calculations rationalize this phase selectivity and the resultant color switching via a kinetic–thermodynamic competition. Doping with antimony and lanthanide enables self-trapped exciton emission, downshifting luminescence, and upconversion luminescence, with the capability of reversible cyclic switching upon structural transformation. Utilizing this capability of reversible color switching in response to external stimuli, two complementary applications are demonstrated: physically unclonable function labels for medicines anti‑counterfeiting, and stimuli‑responsive luminescence for dynamic information encryption (integrating dynamic encoding with a secret-sharing hierarchical authorization framework). Together, these strategies achieve zero‑error authentication and strong cloning resistance. This work establishes rare earth‑based low‑dimensional metal halides as a biomimetic, environment‑interactive system for next‑generation, highly secure anti‑counterfeiting and encryption technologies.

item.title: Disease Mutation‐Guided Discovery of Peptide Inhibitors of the Dyskerin Dimer In H/ACA Ribonucleoproteins
item.description:
Human disease mutations reveal a therapeutically relevant interface within the H/ACA ribonucleoprotein complex. Structure-guided stapled peptides inhibit dyskerin dimerisation and perturb dyskerin-dependent biology, providing proof-of-concept that H/ACA RNP function can be modulated through targeting a previously unexplored protein–protein interaction.


ABSTRACT

Hinge and ACA (H/ACA) ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) play key regulatory roles in ribosome biogenesis, splicing, and telomerase maintenance, and their activities are enhanced in cancer cells. The central component of H/ACA RNPs is the enzyme dyskerin (DKC1). DKC1 has high expression in multiple tumour types, and contributes to cancer hallmarks, tumour growth, and cellular immortalisation. DKC1 mutations also cause dyskeratosis congenita, a premature-ageing syndrome characterised by hindered ribosome biogenesis and shortened telomeres. We leveraged genetic information to devise a strategy to generate dyskerin inhibitors. Mapping of DKC1 mutations on the cryogenic electron microscopy structures of H/ACA RNP showed they alter the dyskerin/dyskerin protein–protein interaction in this complex. Based on this, we designed and synthesised peptides that inhibit dyskerin dimerisation and developed in vitro protein assays demonstrating protein engagement and interaction inhibition. Lead peptides reduced cell viability, protein synthesis, and cancer-related small nucleolar RNA levels in brain tumour cells (medulloblastoma and glioblastoma). Overexpression of DKC1 partially counteracted the effects of peptide inhibitors, consistent with modulation of dyskerin-dependent cellular processes. These results provide proof-of-concept that disruption of the dyskerin/dyskerin interaction can modulate H/ACA RNP function and support exploration of this interface as a potential therapeutic target.

item.title: Sequence‐Retentive Upcycling of Polyamide 66 Into Quasi‐Alternating Biodegradable Polyesteramides With Closed‐Loop Recyclability
item.description:
A one-pot, two-step acidolysis–repolymerization strategy transforms waste polyamide 66 into quasi-alternating biodegradable polyesteramides without full depolymerization to monomers. By preserving amide-rich domains and uniformly inserting hydrolyzable ester linkages, the resulting materials unite high thermal and mechanical performance with tunable enzymatic degradation, aerobic biodegradation, and five-cycle closed-loop recyclability.


ABSTRACT

Polyamide 66 (PA66) is a durable engineering plastic with poor biodegradability and limited energy-efficient recycling options, posing environmental challenges. Herein, we report a sequence-retentive, one-pot, two-step depolymerization-repolymerization strategy for the upcycling of waste PA66 into biodegradable polyesteramides (PA66-EX). Rather than depolymerizing PA66 into constituent monomers, adipic acid-assisted acidolysis selectively converts PA66 into carboxyl-terminated polyamide oligomers with tunable amide sequence lengths, which are reconnected through ester-containing segments via in situ melt polycondensation with ethylene glycol. This sequence-retentive strategy generates quasi-alternating polyesteramide backbones that preserve PA66-derived amide-rich domains while uniformly introducing hydrolysis-sensitive ester linkages. The resulting PA66-EX materials combine biodegradability with high thermal and mechanical performance, showing melting temperatures of 180°C–197°C, 5% mass-loss temperatures above 356°C, tensile strengths of 27–35 MPa, and elongations at break of 414%–745%. Enzymatic degradation increases systematically with ester content, confirming the role of ester linkages as accessible degradation sites. Moreover, PA66-EX demonstrates polymer-to-polymer closed-loop recyclability, largely retaining its molecular sequence characteristics, thermal properties, and mechanical performance over five consecutive, catalyst-free hydrolysis-repolymerization cycles. This work establishes a practical strategy for transforming waste PA66 into high-performance biodegradable polyesteramides and provides a general sequence-retentive molecular design principle for achieving circularity in condensation polymers.

item.title: Sustainable Depolymerization of Polyurethane Waste via Base‐Free Catalytic Hydrogenolysis
item.description:
A supported amorphous molybdenum sulfide catalyst (a-MoS x /Al2O3) is designed for base-free hydrogenation of polyurethane (PU), producing valuable aromatic amines and polyols via an isocyanate pathway.


ABSTRACT

Polyurethane (PU), the sixth most produced polymer globally, poses significant environmental challenges due to its stable cross-linked structure, which hinders degradation and recycling. Although catalytic hydrogenolysis offers a promising route for recovering valuable monomers, current systems generally require strongly alkaline conditions and homogeneous catalysts, limiting their practical applicability. Herein, we report an efficient base-free hydrogenolysis system using a supported amorphous molybdenum sulfide catalyst (a-MoS x /Al2O3) for the closed-loop recycling of PU, achieving recovery rates of 94.6% for aromatic amines and 99.9% for polyols. Mechanistic investigations reveal that abundant sulfur vacancies not only promote the depolymerization of PU to generate isocyanates and polyols, but also catalyze the hydrogenation of isocyanates to amines. This suppresses repolymerization with polyols, ensuring complete depolymerization. The catalyst exhibits broad applicability across diverse PU types and real-world PU waste, while maintaining its activity after regeneration. This work establishes a sustainable catalytic route for converting PU waste into high-value monomers.

item.title: Isolation of Open‐Shell Vinylidene Complexes of Iridium, Ruthenium, and Osmium
item.description:
Open-shell complexes with N-heterocyclic vinylidene ligands have been isolated and characterized. The unpaired electron in these complexes is largely localized on the vinylidene ligand.


ABSTRACT

Open-shell vinylidene complexes are prone to undergo fast, ligand-centered radical reactions. Herein, we describe the synthesis of paramagnetic Ir, Ru, and Os complexes with terminal N-heterocyclic vinylidene ligands. Under inert conditions, these complexes remain stable over extended periods, allowing for isolation on a preparative scale and crystallographic analyses (for Ir and Ru). The results of computational investigations, EPR spectroscopic, and reactivity studies imply that the radical is largely localized on the vinylidene ligand.

item.title: Nitrogen‐Rich Covalent Organic Frameworks Enable Reversible Lithium Deposition in Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
item.description:
A nitrogen-rich COF interphase layer on Cu regulates interfacial Li+ transport and promotes the formation of a stiff, inorganic-rich SEI, thereby supporting dense lithium deposition. This interphase layer enables anode-free lithium batteries to operate at an areal capacity of 4.1 mAh/cm2.


ABSTRACT

Poor lithium reversibility and sluggish interfacial kinetics limit the areal capacity and rate capability of anode-free lithium batteries. A nitrogen-rich covalent organic framework (COF) as an interphase layer promotes uniform lithium deposition, enabling plating/stripping at 20 mAh/cm2 in Li/Cu cells and anode-free full-cell operation at 4.1 mAh/cm2, as reported by Z. Ouyang, S. Zheng, S. Li, et al., Angewandte Chemie Novit 2 (2026): e70027.

item.title: Beyond Lewis Acidity: Thiophilicity and Redox Stability as Design Principles for Sulphur‐Containing Polymerisation Catalysis
item.description:
Sulphur breaks the catalyst rulebook: In sulphur-containing ring-opening copolymerisation, catalysts fail off-cycle, not during propagation. Metal thiolates either bind too tightly or reduce the metal. Two computed descriptors, thiophilicity and redox stability, single out Al(III), delivering high weight polythioesters that can be melt-spun, scCO2-foamed and depolymerised back to phthalic anhydride.


ABSTRACT

Catalysts for the ring-opening copolymerisation (ROCOP) of sulphur-containing monomers are almost invariably inherited from all-oxygen chemistry, where performance tracks the barrier of the rate-determining propagation step. We show that this transfer fails. The activity of Cr(III), Co(III) and Zn(II) complexes of a common salicylimine scaffold cannot be explained by computationally tracking monomer insertions and metal activity is better predicted off-cycle. A revised experimentally supported computational hypothesis implicates metal thiolates, generated by side-reactions at the chain end, to deactivate the catalyst by either binding too tightly to or reducing the metal centre. The resulting computational descriptors, thiophilicity and redox stability, are distinct from Lewis acidity and chemical hardness, and predicted Al(III) to be competent. Al(III) catalysis delivers recyclable sulphur-containing copolymers with a high apparent weight of Mn = 238.6 kg/mol. This unlocks previously underexplored processing methods for these types of materials such as melt-spinning and scCO2-foaming. Our results suggest new structure–activity design rules for sulphur-containing polymerisation catalysis which are urgently required to obtain technologically useful materials.

item.title: Desymmetrization of Acyclic meso‐1,3‐Diols by Cu─H‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Silylation
item.description:
Breaking the symmetry with silicon: a variety of C s -symmetric substrates underwent highly enantioselective monosilylation catalyzed by a Cu─H/(R,R)-Ph-PBE system in the presence of a hydrosilane as the coupling partner. Functional-group incorporation enables access to enantioenriched products bearing versatile reactive handles for subsequent synthetic diversification.


ABSTRACT

A nonenzymatic desymmetrization of acyclic meso-1,3-diols by Si─O coupling with a hydrosilane is reported. The C s -symmetric diols undergo enantioselective monosilylation with a Cu─H/(R,R)-Ph-BPE catalyst system. The choice of hydrosilane was critical for suppressing undesired bissilylation, with a tertiary homobenzylic silane providing the best results. A series of simple alkyl-substituted 1,3-diols was converted into the corresponding silyl ethers with high enantiomeric ratios, with an unsubstituted methylene unit in the 2-position identified as the most favorable scaffold for efficient and selective desymmetrization. Further modifications of the obtained enantioenriched products additionally emphasize the synthetic value of the reported methodology.

item.title: Synergistic Ethylene Glycol Synthesis via Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction Coupled With CH3OH Oxidation
item.description:
Efficient co-upcycling of CO2 and CH3OH into ethylene glycol (EG) is reported via a tandem photocatalytic system, which consists of (i) photoredox catalysis of CO2 reduction integrated with CH3OH coupling over Cu─Zn0.75Cd0.25S catalysts and (ii) photothermal conversion of syngas to CH3OH over commercial CuZnAl catalysts. This tandem system delivers an EG selectivity of 92.5% and a record-high apparent quantum yield of 24.1%.


ABSTRACT

Paired photoredox catalysis enables co-valorization of CO2 and small molecules to high-value chemicals via concurrent oxidation and reduction half-reactions. However, most systems feature decoupled half-reactions with no intrinsic substrate-product interplay, merely utilizing electrons and holes separately, and failing to realize convergent chemical synthesis. Herein, we demonstrate a tandem photoredox-photothermal catalytic system for efficient ethylene glycol (EG) synthesis, comprising (i) the photoredox catalysis of CO2 reduction integrated with C─C coupling of methanol (CH3OH) to EG over Cu-doped Zn0.75Cd0.25S catalysts, and (ii) the photothermal conversion of syngas to CH3OH over commercial CuZnAl catalysts. Of note, the CH3OH formed in situ via CO2 reduction can feed into the pool of oxidation substrates, while the co-generated syngas (ideal H2/CO ratio ≈ 2) is further converted to additional CH3OH and then recirculated as a supplemental oxidation substrate. Such a tandem catalytic design achieves high atom- and redox-economy for EG synthesis, delivering an exceptional apparent quantum yield of 24.1%, outperforming those previously reported for CH3OH coupling to EG under an inert atmosphere. This work highlights the promise of orchestrating photoredox-based closed-loop catalytic architectures for value-added C2+ chemical synthesis with high efficiency and selectivity.

item.title: Membrane‐Fusion Navigated Cell Membrane Anchoring Enhances Pyroptosis for Photoimmunotherapy
item.description:
A membrane-confined photoreaction strategy to directly program pyroptosis was established. Membrane-anchored PBI undergoes in situ photoactivation to generate ROS and protonic acid, synergistically amplifying oxidative membrane damage. By shifting design paradigm from photosensitizer molecular engineering to spatial regulation of cellular reactions, this work identifies the plasma membrane as an active platform for photoimmunotherapy.


ABSTRACT

Pyroptosis, a membrane disruptive and highly immunogenic form of programmed cell death, remains underexploited in cancer photoimmunotherapy due to the lack of general design principles beyond photosensitizer engineering. Here, we establish a membrane confined strategy that directly programs pyroptotic execution by targeting the plasma membrane as the primary reaction interface. A membrane fusogenic liposomal system enables precise anchoring of a caged perylene bisimides (PBI) onto the cell membrane, bypassing complex molecular modification. Upon light irradiation, PBI undergoes photocyclization to generate an active photosensitizer (CBI) and a protonic acid in situ. This dual output synergistically amplifies reactive oxygen species (ROS) production within a confined lipid environment, promoting lipid peroxidation, GPX4 downregulation, and membrane destabilization. Consequently, pyroptosis is efficiently triggered alongside ferroptosis, leading to enhanced tumor cell killing and immune activation both in vitro and in vivo. By shifting the design paradigm from molecular optimization to cell membrane control, this work reframes the plasma membrane from a passive barrier into an active reaction platform, providing a general and modular strategy for programmable pyroptosis-based photoimmunotherapy.

item.title: Ferroelectric‐Field Gating Suppresses the Outward Migration of Active Oxygen Intermediates in Li‐Rich Cathodes
item.description:
Ferroelectric polarization establishes a built-in electric field that counteracts the concentration-gradient-driven outward migration of negatively charged oxygen intermediates in Li-rich layered oxide cathodes. This electrostatic gating suppresses the interfacial accumulation of peroxide/superoxide-like species and irreversible oxygen evolution, thereby enhancing oxygen-redox reversibility and structural stability.


ABSTRACT

Li-rich layered oxides deliver high capacities through cation–anion co-redox chemistry. During high-voltage charging, however, peroxide/superoxide-like O─O intermediates migrate down their concentration gradient from oxygen-redox-active regions toward particle surfaces, accumulating at the interface. This accumulation accelerates irreversible O2 evolution and structural degradation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and rapid capacity fading. Here, we construct a spontaneously polarized ferroelectric LiNbO3 interfacial layer that generates a built-in electric field to regulate oxygen redox in Li-rich cathodes. This electric field suppresses concentration-gradient-driven migration and interfacial enrichment of charged active oxygen intermediates, limiting O2 evolution and preserving a uniform surface-to-bulk distribution of oxygen electronic states at high delithiation. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 310 mAh g−1, an initial Coulombic efficiency of 99.97%, and 79% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, this strategy enables Li-metal pouch cells to achieve an energy density of 620 Wh kg−1 and graphite-based pouch cells to maintain stable operation over 2000 cycles. This work establishes ferroelectric-field regulation as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxygen redox chemistry in Li-rich cathodes.

item.title: An Expandable Library of Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium‐Metal Batteries
item.description:
A chemically diverse solid polymer electrolyte library enables systematic correlations between polymer chemistry and electrochemical behavior. Library-based screening identifies promising building blocks for compositionally complex SPEs, exemplified by poly(EA-FMA-VA) with outstanding electrochemical performance.


ABSTRACT

Solid-polymer-electrolytes (SPEs) offer alternatives to next-generation solid-state lithium-metal batteries, promising advantages in mechanical-compliance, processability, cost-effectiveness, and safety. While tremendous efforts have generated diverse SPEs since 1970s, SPE-practicality remains limited by the trade-offs among ion-conductivity, high-voltage stability, and Li0-electrolyte compatibility. Here, we establish the first SPE library covering 12 SPEs across five polymer families, which allows us to collect large datasets on chemistry, interfacial, and electrochemical properties that unveil their hidden connections. Correlation analysis of these descriptors reveals binding-strength between polymer and Li+, subtle variations in polymer molecular structure, and solid-electrolyte-interphase composition as dictating factors. Also discovered is that the standard deviation of coulombic-efficiency rather than its average value governs the battery cycling stability. The SPE library can be rapidly expanded through two structural engineering pathways: grafting diverse functional segments onto backbones and constructing compositionally-complex SPEs. As a proof-of-concept, we fabricate several such SPEs and find improved high-voltage stability through gradually increasing the complexity of the polymer matrices. A terpolymer-based acrylates SPE exhibits outstanding Li0 plating/stripping over 1800 h, stable cycling in LiCoO2||Li battery with 100% capacity retention and an average coulombic-efficiency of 99.91% ± 0.09% over 100 cycles. This work provides a transformative framework to design the future polymer materials.

item.title: Ring‐Retaining Polymerization of Vinylidenecyclopropanes
item.description:
Organonickel catalysts with coordinating counterions enable C2 ring-retaining polymerization of commodity feedstock-derived vinylidenecyclopropanes (VDCPs). Strain-releasing alkene coordination is the key.


ABSTRACT

Commodity feedstock-derived vinylidenecyclopropanes (VDCPs) are a new class of allenic monomers stereoelectronically intermediate between butatrienes and allenes. While their butatriene character drives the C5 ring-opening polymerization (C5-ROP), the complementary allene-type polymerization mode remains elusive. Herein we report this new pathway for VDCPs. Organonickel catalysts with coordinating counterions enable C2 ring-retaining polymerization (C2-RRP), yielding pendant alkylidenecyclopropane moieties. Computations ascribe this reactivity to strain-release alkene coordination, which further enables one-pot diblock copolymerization with conventional allenes.

item.title: MitoDART: Mitochondria‐Targeted Intracellular DNA Assembly for Selective Mitochondrial Interference and Early Molecular Response Monitoring
item.description:
In this study, we report a mitochondria-targeted dual-biomarker-activated intracellular DNA assembly for mitochondrial regulation and tracking (Mito-DART), which enables cell-selective mitochondrial interference and in situ monitoring of early molecular responses following mitochondrial disruption.


ABSTRACT

Rational modulation of mitochondrial functions to reprogram cellular behavior and fate has emerged as a promising therapeutic paradigm. However, it is still challenging to achieve cell-selective mitochondrial interference with in situ monitoring of early molecular responses. In this study, we report a mitochondria-targeted dual-biomarker-activated intracellular DNA assembly for mitochondrial regulation and tracking (Mito-DART), which enables cell-selective interference of mitochondria and in situ biosensing for early assessment of molecular responses. Based on the AND logic responsive to two tumor biomarkers, apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) and microRNAs, Mito-DART is specifically activated in tumor cells and undergoes hybridization chain reaction (HCR)-driven DNA assembly, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis-associated cellular responses. More importantly, Mito-DART enables in situ monitoring of cytochrome c (Cyt c) release, an early molecular marker of mitochondria-mediated apoptosis, within 1 h following mitochondrial disruption, providing an early molecular readout of mitochondria-mediated apoptotic signaling that complements conventional tissue-level endpoint assessments. Overall, this design provides a programmable framework for biomarker-gated mitochondrial intervention that combines selective activation with built-in assessment of downstream molecular responses.

item.title: Hofmeister Engineering Enables High‐Voltage Aqueous All‐Organic Batteries
item.description:
An aqueous all-organic battery combining a PTCDI anode with an organic bromine cathode achieves a high-discharge voltage of 2.0 V through reversible Br−/Br0/Br+ conversion, together with high-energy and power densities. The battery accommodates diverse charge carriers, while electrolyte anions regulate electrode reversibility and kinetics through the Hofmeister effect, and cations primarily govern reaction kinetics.


ABSTRACT

Aqueous all-organic batteries (AOBs) offer a safe and sustainable alternative for electrochemical energy storage, yet their energy density is constrained by the limited availability of organic redox couples with high-working voltages. Here we develop a versatile redox couple by pairing a 3,4,9,10-perylenetetracarboxylic diimide (PTCDI) anode with a quaternary-ammonium bromine cathode, enabling an initial discharge voltage of up to 2.0 V through reversible two-electron bromine conversion (Br−/Br0/Br+). This battery chemistry is compatible with diverse charge carriers, including Li+, Na+, K+, NH4 +, Ca2+, and Mg2+. We further reveal that electrolyte ions exert distinct effects on electrode reactions: Cations primarily regulate reaction kinetics, whereas anions govern both reversibility and kinetics through the Hofmeister effect. Kosmotropic anions suppress polybromide dissolution and improve reversibility, but retard electrode kinetics, while chaotropic anions facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of active-material retention. Guided by this mechanistic insight, a hybrid kosmotropic/chaotropic electrolyte balances these competing effects. The optimized one-electron configuration retains 83.1% of its capacity after 12 000 cycles, while the two-electron configuration delivers an energy density of approximately 107 Wh kg−1 based on the combined electrode active-material mass. High areal capacities exceeding 4 mAh cm−2 further demonstrate its practical potential. This work establishes electrolyte solvation engineering as an effective strategy for high-energy AOBs.

item.title: Electrochemical PVC Recycling Unlocks Efficient Ring‐Closure Toward Amine‐Bearing Ketene Acetals as Novel Monomers for Poly(Amino Ester) Synthesis
item.description:
A paired electrochemical PVC upcycling strategy combines cathodic dechlorination with anodic synthesis of novel nitrogen-containing cyclic acetals as precursors for poly(amino ester) synthesis. Experimental and computational studies reveal that heteroatoms strongly influence cyclization efficiencies of medium-sized rings. The methodology unlocks access to biodegradable poly(amino ester) homo- and copolymer synthesis via radical ring-opening polymerization.


ABSTRACT

A paired electrochemical synthetic strategy for the upcycling of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is reported, enabling simultaneous cathodic dechlorination of the polymer backbone and anodic formation of cyclic halo acetals (CHAs) as monomer precursors. The process channels liberated chloride into cyclic acetal structures, which are converted into cyclic ketene acetals and subsequently polymerized via radical ring-opening polymerization (rROP) to access degradable polyester and poly(amino ester) materials. Electrochemical cyclization unlocks the synthesis of previously unavailable nitrogen-containing cyclic ketene acetal monomers in remarkably high yields. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal a pronounced heteroatom effect on cyclization efficiency, attributed to conformational preorganization induced by an increasing gauche effect upon ether and amide incorporation. A nitrogen-containing ketene acetal monomer was polymerized and copolymerized with established ketene acetals, affording new functional, biodegradable polymer materials. Successful copolymerization with methyl acrylate demonstrates the incorporation of hydrolysable moieties into otherwise persistent olefinic materials. Importantly, cathodic PVC dechlorination proceeds independently of the anodic transformation, highlighting the broad applicability of this paired-electrolysis strategy in an undivided cell. Overall, this work establishes a versatile electrochemical PVC recycling process while simultaneously generating previously inaccessible monomer building blocks for biodegradable polymer synthesis.

item.title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Sharpless Asymmetric Dihydroxylation With Expanded Substrate Compatibility
item.description:
The first mechanochemical protocol for the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation is reported. A wide range of alkenes underwent highly efficient enantioselective dihydroxylation under ball-milling conditions, typically reaching completion within 30 min to afford the corresponding chiral diols in good to high yield with excellent enantioselectivity.


ABSTRACT

The Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation is an established transformation in organic synthesis for the preparation of chiral vicinal diols. However, conventional biphasic solution-based conditions (typically water/t-BuOH) require long reaction times (up to ∼48 h) and large amounts of solvent. Moreover, they often exhibit limited substrate scope due to low solubility of the substrates and functional-group incompatibility. Herein, we report the first mechanochemical protocol for the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation, which affords the desired diols with excellent enantioselectivity, comparable to that of conventional methods. Notably, most substrates are fully converted within 30 min without the need for large quantities of solvent. Moreover, the mechanochemical conditions enable efficient reactions of substrates that are challenging to convert under solution-based conditions, including poorly soluble, base-sensitive, and catalyst-coordinating compounds. The practical utility of this protocol is further demonstrated by the efficient dihydroxylation of an intermediate of a natural product and a gram-scale synthesis.

item.title: A General Strategy to Identify Impurity‐Activated Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Synthetic Triarylamines
item.description:
A sequential diagnostic framework integrating synthetic-route validation, chromatographic fractionation, purification, impurity identification, and reconstitution is established to distinguish intrinsic RTP from impurity-derived emission in synthetic triarylamines. Trace C–H arylation byproducts generated during synthesis are identified as a major class of triplet-energy traps that activate RTP of the synthesized triarylamines.


ABSTRACT

Distinguishing intrinsic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) from impurity-derived emission remains challenging in organic luminescent materials, particularly when trace emissive species evade routine characterization. Herein, we establish a diagnostic framework for identifying impurity-activated RTP in synthetic triarylamines through route-, fraction-, and purification-dependent validation, impurity reconstitution, and theoretical analysis. Using TPA, TPAO, and related heteroatom-engineered triarylamines as representative systems, we show that nominally identical samples can exhibit different RTP behaviors depending on synthetic history and purification extent, despite appearing chemically indistinguishable by conventional analyses. Progressive purification induces blue-shifted and narrowed emissions and ultimately eliminates afterglow, revealing hidden emissive species. Structural analyses identify trace C–H arylation byproducts generated during metal-catalyzed coupling reactions as a representative class of RTP-active impurities. Reintroduction of independently synthesized impurity candidates into rigorously purified hosts restores phosphorescence, providing direct functional evidence that synthesis-derived byproducts can activate RTP. Theoretical calculations further show that these impurities possess lower-lying triplet states and act as triplet-energy traps. Extension of the workflow to related synthetic triarylamines reproduces purification-dependent RTP loss and impurity-enabled recovery, supporting the applicability of this strategy across the triarylamine systems examined here and establishing synthetic history and purification as critical variables in assigning the origin of organic RTP.

item.title: Tailoring the Na+ Transport Microenvironment With an Anion‐Capturing Interface Enables Low‐Temperature, Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
item.description:
A phosphorus-rich interphase on NP-HC captures PF6 − anions near the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP), creating an anion-rich interfacial environment. This tailored interface promotes rapid Na+ desolvation and accelerates interfacial ion-migration kinetics, overcoming sluggish desolvation and transport in conventional hard carbon (HC) and enabling improved low-temperature electrochemical performance.


ABSTRACT

Na+ desolvation and diffusion across the solid-electrolyte interface (SEI) are two bottlenecks to fast charging at low temperatures in hard-carbon sodium-ion batteries. Here, we design an anion-capturing interface that provides a customized interfacial environment to enhance interfacial dynamics at low temperatures. We demonstrate that phosphate can promote the formation of a homogeneous inorganic SEI by inducing anion enrichment near the inner Helmholtz plane. The phosphorus-rich interface exhibits multiple benefits, including the formation of a built-in electric field and a reduced energy barrier for Na+ interphase diffusion. The hard carbon–phosphate interface (NP-HC) anode maintains a capacity of 183.6 mAh g−1 at 0.5 A g−1 (−30°C). The pouch cell utilizing the NP-HC anode achieves a 90.2% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at a 2 C rate. Even so, NP-HC pouch cells can operate stably even at temperatures as low as −40°C, indicating their potential to enhance the performance of sodium-ion batteries under harsh conditions.

item.title: Molecular Crystal Phase Transformation via Nonclassical Pathways: Surfactant‐Based Kinetic Control of Metastable Amorphous Intermediates
item.description:
Water-induced phase transformations challenge molecular crystals stability, yet their pathways remain elusive. Using piroxicam as a model, a multistage pathway is revealed where an amorphous phase serves as a critical intermediate. Targeting this intermediate, enables kinetic control of transformation by surfactant chain length. This work establishes a foundation for rational design of additives to regulate phase behavior in organic crystals.


ABSTRACT

Molecular crystals serve as essential components in a wide range of functional products, yet their performance is often compromised by unpredictable phase transformations, particularly in aqueous environments. Although nonclassical, multistage pathways are frequently proposed for such transitions, the specific role of transient intermediates remains poorly understood. Here, we employ in situ atomic force microscopy and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy to elucidate a nonclassical transformation pathway in the model molecular crystal piroxicam that proceeds via metastable intermediates. These intermediates serve as amorphous precursors that undergo densification prior to crystallization, facilitating a rapid transition from the anhydrate to a less soluble hydrate phase. The onset and kinetics of this transformation are tunable through the use of cationic surfactants with varying alkyl-chain lengths. Longer-chain surfactants cooperatively adsorb onto both dissolving crystal facets and nanodroplets in solution, creating a dense interfacial barrier that delays precursor formation and subsequent crystallization. This work presents a strategy to manipulate phase transformation pathways in molecular crystals by targeting the metastable intermediates via tailored additive-interface interactions, enabling the predictive design of advanced materials with controlled phase behavior and enhanced performance reliability.

item.title: Built‐in Electric Field Modulating Interfacial Charge Dynamics in V2AlC‐Derived Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterostructures for Broadband Microwave Absorption
item.description:
Built-in electric fields are constructed at the heterogeneous interfaces of V2AlC-derived magnetic-dielectric composites to modulate interfacial charge dynamics. These fields enhance multiple polarization, optimize impedance matching, and strengthen attenuation. Consequently, the heterostructures achieve a broad effective absorption bandwidth of 6.72 GHz and a minimum reflection loss of −48.3 dB.


ABSTRACT

The tailored design of magnetic-dielectric heterostructures offers considerable potential for high-performance electromagnetic wave absorption, yet achieving efficient interfacial charge separation remains challenging. Herein, we constructed VC/FeCoNi/Al2O3 heterostructures with built-in electric fields (BIEFs) via the topological structural transformation of V2AlC in Lewis acidic molten salts. This transformation involves the redox-potential-driven substitution by Fe/Co/Ni cations, leading to in situ alloying within the VC interlayers to balance the electromagnetic parameters. Theoretical calculations reveal that the work-function difference drives directional interfacial charge redistribution, as evidenced by experimental observations of charge transfer and surface-potential differences. This charge redistribution reconstructs the local electronic states, leading to interfacial orbital hybridization and establishing BIEFs at the heterointerfaces. Atomic vacancies and lattice distortions generated during etching, coupled with the BIEFs, enhance interfacial and defect-induced polarization. Consequently, the optimized composite achieves a wide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.72 GHz (at 1.7 mm) and a minimum reflection loss of −48.3 dB (at 2.8 mm). This BIEF-mediated interfacial engineering strategy offers a viable route for designing high-performance broadband microwave absorbers.

item.title: Unlocking Intrinsic Narrowband Organic Ultralong Afterglow Through Efficient Two‐Photon Ionization
item.description:
This work demonstrates an effective strategy to achieve narrowband organic ultralong afterglow by harnessing localized excitons of guests through efficient two-photon ionization. Through engineering multiresonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence guests, the full-color narrowband OUA emissions with full width at half maximum (FWHM) as narrow as 30 nm and unprecedentedly long durations exceeding 44 hours are achieved.


ABSTRACT

Organic ultralong afterglow (OUA) materials are exclusively constrained by their reliance on host–guest exciplexes, which inherently suffer from spectral broadening and limited color tunability. Here we demonstrate an effective strategy to achieve narrowband OUA by harnessing localized excitons of guests through efficient two-photon ionization (TPI). Through engineering multi-resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) guests, we achieve full-color narrowband OUA emissions with full width at half maximum (FWHM) as narrow as 30 nm and unprecedentedly long durations exceeding 44 hours, which are comparable to commercial inorganic afterglow materials. The rigid planar molecular architecture of MR-TADF not only promotes TPI but also reinforces host–guest interactions, thus fostering efficient charge separation to boost OUA properties. The intrinsic OUA can also be achieved based on fluorophore and metal–organic complex guests with planar molecular skeletons. The resultant materials enable promising applications in spectrally pure emergency afterglow lighting and sophisticated afterglow organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). The afterglow OLEDs exhibit a maximum luminance of 26481 cd/m2, an external quantum efficiency of 8.7%, and record-breaking ultralong electroluminescence afterglow lasting over 15 minutes. Our findings establish a valuable design principle for modulating charge migration and exciton transitions towards developing next-generation OUA materials.

item.title: Revealing Oxidation‐State‐Dependent Selectivity in Urea Electrosynthesis Over Stabilized Co/CoOx Surfaces
item.description:
Cobalt-based model catalysts are designed to investigate their oxidation-state-dependent catalytic roles during urea electrosynthesis from CO2 and NO2 −. Cr3+ retards CoO x over-reduction, stabilizing a non-equilibrium Co/CoO x working surface. Our results suggest a spatially coupled reaction network: metallic Co tends to form CO2-derived *CO, CoO x motifs may generate *NH2, and their interface is inferred to facilitate *CO–*NH2 coupling toward urea.


ABSTRACT

Electrocatalytic upgrading of CO2 and nitrogen wastes offers a sustainable route for urea synthesis, yet its selectivity is limited by competing parallel reactions and operando catalyst reconstruction. Here, using cobalt-based model catalysts, we demonstrate that product partitioning among competing pathways can be selectively directed by metallic and oxidized cobalt phases. By introducing oxophilic Cr3+ to retard cathodic over-reduction of cobalt oxides, we stabilize a non-equilibrium Co/CoO x surface under working conditions. The optimized Co@CoO x -Cr1 catalyst achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency of 40.1 ± 1.1% and a yield rate of 102.27 ± 3.31 mmol h−1 gcat −1 under pressurized CO2 at −0.3 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support a proposed oxidation-state-dependent relay mechanism in which metallic Co favors CO2-to-*CO conversion, stabilized CoO x motifs may promote *NH2 formation, and their interface is inferred to facilitate *CO─*NH2 coupling for urea formation. This work identifies the controlled stabilization of coexisting phases with distinct oxidation states as a strategy for steering selectivity in multi-reactant electrocatalysis.

item.title: Single‐Vesicle Membrane Order‐Resolved Super‐Resolution Imaging Reveals Cholesterol Enrichment and Its Functional Role in Extracellular Vesicle Uptake
item.description:
Spectrally resolved single-molecule imaging of Nile Red enables membrane-order analysis at the single-vesicle level, revealing substantial heterogeneity in cholesterol content among extracellular vesicles.


ABSTRACT

Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are heterogeneous in membrane composition, yet conventional lipid analysis cannot resolve individual vesicles. Here we develop membrane order-resolved, spectrally encoded super-resolution imaging to simultaneously quantify membrane order and size at the single-EV level. Combining Nile Red single-molecule spectroscopy with localization microscopy achieves ∼30 nm resolution and reveals pronounced vesicle-to-vesicle heterogeneity. Using defined liposomes, cholesterol enrichment, and pharmacological inhibition, we establish membrane order as a sensitive surrogate for relative cholesterol content in individual EVs. Application to EVs from breast, gastric, and oral cell lines reveals cell-type- and tissue-dependent differences. Most cancer-cell-derived EVs show higher membrane order and higher inferred cholesterol than non-tumor counterparts, although MDA-MB-231 EVs are an exception. Functional assays demonstrate that increasing EV membrane cholesterol enhances cellular uptake and shifts internalization from clathrin-mediated to non-clathrin-mediated pathways. These findings identify cholesterol enrichment as a frequent feature of cancer-cell-derived EVs and link membrane composition to uptake efficiency and pathway selection. This work provides a single-EV analytical platform and new insight into how membrane lipid heterogeneity regulates EV-mediated intercellular communication.

item.title: Supramolecular Iron(II)‐Anchored Porphyrin Glycoassemblies Enable Galectin‐Targeted Photodynamic Therapy
item.description:
Coordination-driven self-assembly integrates multivalent lectin recognition, porphyrin-based photosensitization, and aqueous solubility within a single, well-defined nanocage, enabling galectin-targeted photodynamic activity in cancer cells.


ABSTRACT

Photodynamic therapy (PDT) relies on photosensitizers that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon light irradiation to trigger cytotoxic effects in target tissues. Porphyrins are among the most widely used PDT photosensitizers due to their strong visible-light absorption and efficient ROS generation, although their broad application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation, and limited selectivity. Here, Fe(II)-anchored porphyrin nanocages displaying peripheral lactose residues were prepared by coordination-driven subcomponent self-assembly to combine photodynamic activity with multivalent glycan presentation. The resulting cubic Fe8L6 architectures were characterized by NMR spectroscopy, UV–vis spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and transmission electron microscopy. The zinc-metalated porphyrin nanoassembly, [1-Zn][BF4]16, generated both singlet oxygen and superoxide upon red-light irradiation, providing access to multiple ROS pathways. Isothermal titration calorimetry revealed high-affinity binding to galectin-3 (K d = 2.65 ± 0.26 µM), a lectin commonly upregulated in epithelial cancers. A549 cells treated with [1-Zn][BF4]16 exhibited potent light-induced cytotoxicity with negligible dark toxicity, with a phototoxicity index (PI) of 55, while pre-treatment with lactose or thiodigalactose was protective against [1-Zn][BF4]16 toxicity. These results demonstrate that coordination-driven self-assembly provides an effective strategy for integrating multivalent lectin recognition and photodynamic activity within a single nanoscale architecture.

item.title: Boosting DMF Electrosynthesis Over Bifunctional NiCo Catalysts via Methanol‐Supplemented *CHO Supply
item.description:
This work developed a NiCo bimetallic catalyst that undergoes in situ reconstruction to form NiOOH/CoOOH dual active sites for efficient DMF synthesis from methanol and DMA (56% FE, 518 µmol cm−2 h−1, 105 h stability), with methanol supplying additional *CHO source to boost C−N coupling.


ABSTRACT

Traditional industrial routes for N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) synthesis typically require harsh conditions of high temperature and pressure, leading to high energy consumption and a large carbon footprint. Electrosynthesis of DMF has emerged as a sustainable alternative; however, this pathway still faces the challenges of low activity and poor selectivity. In this study, we present an efficient bifunctional NiCo electrocatalyst synthesized via the electrodeposition method. This catalyst achieves a DMF Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 56% with a production rate of 518 µmol cm−2 h−1. Combined in situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that NiOOH and CoOOH species act as potent oxygen-transfer mediators, facilitating N–H bond activation and dehydrogenation of dimethylamine (DMA). These species also promote C–N coupling between the *N(CH3)2 intermediate and *CHO intermediates derived from both methanol and the self-decomposition of DMA. Furthermore, we find that the introduction of methanol provides a sufficient supply of *CHO intermediates, thereby further enhancing the selectivity of DMF synthesis compared with using DMA as the sole substrate. This work not only identifies the origin of the *CHO donor and its pivotal function in DMF electrosynthesis but also provides a foundation for designing multicomponent synergistic catalysts for advanced electrosynthesis.

item.title: Photocatalytic PVDF Degradation Coupled With Catalytic Targeted Li Replenishment Toward Low‐Energy Repair of Spent LiFePO4 Electrodes
item.description:
We proposed a photocatalytic strategy toward low-energy repair of spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP) materials. Supported by theoretical analysis and in-situ characterizations, TiO2 can generate photogenerated electron–hole pairs synchronously under UV irradiation for degradation of PVDF and targeted Li replenishment of LFP. The repaired LFP material with 2.5 mol% maintained 98.3% capacity retention ratio after 1500 cycles.


ABSTRACT

Directly repair is recognized as a promising route for recycling spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP), but it is challenged by uneven Li supplementation and high energy input. Herein, we propose a photocatalytic strategy for PVDF degradation coupled with targeted Li replenishment toward low-energy repair of spent LFP materials. Supported by theoretical analysis and in-situ characterizations, TiO2 can generate photogenerated electron–hole pairs synchronously under UV irradiation. The photogenerated holes promote the formation of •OH radicals, which abstract hydrogen atoms from the methylene units in PVDF, triggering the scission of polymer backbones and thus enabling the effective degradation of PVDF. Meanwhile, the photogenerated electrons accumulated on TiO2 create a strong reductive microenvironment conducive to the reduction of Fe3+ to Fe2+, which reduces the Li+ migration barrier and facilitates lithium replenishment. The TiO2 catalyst can incorporate into the material lattice as a favorable dopant to optimize the performances of as-repaired LFP material. Specially, the repaired LFP material with 2.5 mol% TiO2 delivers a high discharge capacity of 140.6 mAh g−1 at 1 C with 99.8% capacity retention ratio after 100 cycles. Even at a high rate of 5 C, it maintains 98.3% capacity retention ratio over 1500 cycles.

item.title: An Artificial Phosphoinositide Phosphatase Inhibiting Pyroptosis Cascade for Sepsis Treatment
item.description:
Terbium-doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) act as artificial pan-PIP phosphatases, dephosphorylating plasma-membrane phosphoinositides to block GSDMD pore formation and inflammasome activation. TCNs suppress pyroptotic cytokine release and improve survival in murine endotoxemic sepsis, establishing nanoparticle-mediated PIP modulation as a strategy for precision pyroptosis attenuation.


ABSTRACT

Sepsis mortality remains largely driven by dysregulated pyroptosis, where gasdermin D (GSDMD) pores release lethal cytokines via phosphoinositide (PIP)-mediated membrane recruitment. To disrupt this process, we engineer terbium-doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) with sublattice-induced oxygen vacancies and optimized Ce3+/Ce4+ ratios, functioning as artificial phosphatases that achieve > 20-fold enhanced dephosphorylation activity against the model substrate (para-nitrophenyl phosphate) versus pristine nanoparticles. Mechanistically, TCNs dephosphorylate PIPs at the plasma membrane, disrupting the canonical pyroptosis cascade by simultaneously interfering with inflammasome activation and the N-terminal domain of GSDMD (GSDMD-NT) oligomerization, ultimately inhibiting lytic pore formation. This pan-PIP dephosphorylation approach overcomes the limitations of natural phosphatases by enabling efficient lipid dephosphorylation and preventing GSDMD membrane localization. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrate that TCNs significantly reduce pro-inflammatory cytokine release and improve survival rates in a murine model of endotoxemic sepsis. This work establishes nanoparticle-mediated PIP modulation as a potential strategy for sepsis immunotherapy, rebalancing immune homeostasis through precision pyroptosis attenuation.

item.title: Programmable Skeletal Editing of Pyridines Into Regiodefined N‐Alkyl Pyrazoles
item.description:
Pyridines are remodeled into regiodefined N-alkyl pyrazoles through amine-mediated ring opening and selective two-carbon extrusion. Preinstallation of the N-alkyl group programs product regiochemistry, enabling precise ring-to-ring skeletal editing and late-stage access to pyrazole analogues of pyridine-containing drugs.


ABSTRACT

N-Alkyl pyrazoles are common motifs in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their preparation as single regioisomers is often hampered by poor regioselectivity in the direct alkylation of NH-pyrazoles. Here we report a skeletal-editing strategy that converts readily available pyridines into regiodefined N-alkyl pyrazoles through selective two-carbon deletion. The N-substituent is installed before pyrazole formation and retained through amine-mediated Zincke-type ring opening, acid-promoted cyclization, and retro-Mannich extrusion of a two-carbon enamine, fixing the pyrazole regiochemistry at the precursor stage. The sequence contracts the C5N pyridine framework into a C3N2 pyrazole, transferring the ring nitrogen, three carbon atoms, and their substitution pattern directly onto the product. The method accommodates diverse pyridine scaffolds and N-alkyl groups and enables the skeletal remodeling of structurally complex molecules, transforming a problematic regioselective N-alkylation into a programmable precursor-design strategy.

item.title: Interfacial State‐Perturbed Triplet Energy Transfer in Dye‐Sensitized Upconversion Nanoparticles for Early HIV Diagnosis
item.description:
Subtle perturbation of the interfacial binding of Cypate on sub-7 nm UCNPs dramatically modulates triplet energy transfer (TET) efficiency, resulting in a highly sensitive upconversion luminescence (UCL) response. Leveraging this signal-transduction superiority, the TET-sensitized UCL immunosorbent assay (TET-ULISA) achieves a signal-to-background ratio of 375 and enables femtogram-level p24 detection, providing a versatile and ultrasensitive platform for trace biomarker detection.


ABSTRACT

Early diagnosis of HIV infection is pivotal for curbing AIDS progression and enabling timely therapeutic interventions. However, current immunoassays remain constrained by inadequate sensitivity for detecting trace levels of the HIV-1 p24 antigen during the seroconversion window period. In this study, we discover that subtle perturbations in the interfacial binding state of a carboxylated near-infrared dye, Cypate, on sub-7 nm NaGdF4:Yb3+/Er3+ upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) dramatically modulate triplet energy transfer (TET) efficiency, resulting in a remarkable upconversion luminescence (UCL) response with a signal-to-background ratio as high as 375. By leveraging this interfacial state-perturbed TET as a signal transduction model, we further develop a TET-sensitized UCL immunosorbent assay (TET-ULISA) for HIV-1 p24 antigen detection. In this platform, the target p24 triggers alkaline phosphatase (ALP) to generate phosphate ions, which competitively displace Cypate from the UCNP surface, disrupting TET and producing a dramatic UCL response. The resulting TET-ULISA exhibits high sensitivity for p24 antigen with a limit of detection as low as 112 fg mL−1, representing an 860-fold improvement over the corresponding ALP-based method by employing the identical immunoassay steps, thus enabling early HIV diagnosis within the critical serological window period.

item.title: Selective Gas‐Phase Photocatalytic Methane‐to‐Methanol Conversion Over Gallium Oxynitride With Molecular Oxygen as the Sole Oxidant
item.description:
Selective gas-phase methane oxidation to methanol is achieved over Ag-decorated GaON/GaN using molecular oxygen or untreated room air. Partial surface oxidation promotes O2 activation, while residual –NH groups regulate oxygen-derived reactive intermediates, suppressing methanol overoxidation to CO2. This cooperative surface chemistry enables efficient methane-to-methanol conversion with high methanol selectivity and production rates.


ABSTRACT

Selective oxidation of methane to methanol using molecular oxygen remains challenging because methane activation is often accompanied by deep oxidation of the desired methanol product. Here we report a metal-decorated, partially oxidized GaON/GaN photocatalyst for gas-phase methane-to-methanol conversion using molecular oxygen as the oxidant. The optimized Ag/GaON/GaN catalyst delivers a methane oxidation rate of 2.6 mmol g− 1 h− 1 with ∼85% CH4-to-CH3OH selectivity under O2. When untreated room air is used as the oxidant in a closed-loop recirculating system, the catalyst maintains an activity of 1.0–1.3 mmol g− 1 h− 1 in a 50 h test, with comparable methanol selectivity. Complementary mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support a mechanism in which partial surface oxidation promotes O2 activation, while residual surface –NH species may moderate the resulting reactive intermediates through local H-transfer processes, thereby suppressing methanol overoxidation. These results highlight partially oxidized oxynitride surfaces as a promising platform for selective methane upgrading under gas-phase photocatalytic conditions.

item.title: Anion‐Anchoring, Anti‐Swelling Polymer Interphase Enables Durable Lithium Metal Anodes in Localized High‐Concentration Electrolytes
item.description:
A dual-functional artificial interphase featuring tethered imidazolium cations for electrostatic anion anchoring and long aliphatic side chains for anti-swelling addresses the critical failure of polymer coatings in localized high-concentration electrolytes.


ABSTRACT

Localized high-concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) can improve the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries by promoting anion-rich solvation structures that favor the formation of inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs). However, their favorable interfacial chemistry is not self-sustaining because the native SEI is heterogeneous and prone to repeated rupture during Li plating/stripping, thus progressively depleting active Li and electrolyte. Polymeric artificial SEIs have emerged as a complementary strategy for interfacial stabilization, but their effectiveness in LHCEs is limited by an inherent conflict: the polar functional groups that coordinate ions also coordinate solvents, causing polymer swelling, dissolution, and disruption of anion-rich solvation structures. Here, we develop an anion-anchoring and anti-swelling artificial SEI (AS–SEI) by integrating imidazolium cations with long aliphatic side chains. Imidazolium cations enable anion anchoring to sustain the LHCE-favored anion-rich environment at the interface, while long aliphatic chains provide anti-swelling behavior that protects anchoring sites from competitive solvation. Consequently, AS-SEI exhibits a high Young's modulus (5.0–10.5 GPa) and a high Li+ transference number (0.94), while promoting the formation of LiF/Li2O-rich SEIs. Li||Cu cells achieve 480 cycles with 99.5% average Coulombic efficiency, while Li||NCM811 cells deliver ∼900 cycles with 80% capacity retention (a nearly threefold improvement), with the strategy remaining effective across ether-, ester-, and sulfone-based LHCEs.

item.title: Toward a Visible‐Range Helicity Filter: Panchromatic Magnetic Circular Dichroism via 4f‐Orbital‐Based Charge Transfer in a Cerium(IV) Complex
item.description:
Conceptual illustration of a magnetic circular dichroism (MCD)-based light-helicity filter using a tetravalent cerium complex. The complex exhibits MCD signals spanning the visible spectrum with a sign reversal at ∼520 nm, providing a molecular approach toward panchromatic helicity filters using a single molecular species.


ABSTRACT

Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD)-based light-helicity filters provide a material-based approach to controlling the helicity of light. However, helicity control across the entire visible spectrum using a single molecular species has not yet been demonstrated. Herein, we report a tetravalent cerium (Ce(IV)) complex exhibiting panchromatic MCD properties originating from 4f-orbital-based ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) transitions. A Ce(IV) complex containing four electron-donating anionic diethyldithiocarbamate ligands was synthesized. This complex exhibits panchromatic light absorption with both positive (520–780 nm) and negative (380–520 nm) MCD signals. Relativistic time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT) calculations reveal that this panchromatic light absorption originates from multiple LMCT transitions. The strong spin-orbit coupling (SOC) associated with the Ce(IV) 4f orbitals facilitates the mixing of singlet and triplet LMCT excited states, enabling panchromatic light absorption. The 4f-orbital-based transition properties also contribute to effective MCD signals governed by the Faraday B-term. These findings highlight the potential of panchromatic MCD in a Ce(IV) complex as a promising approach toward the development of visible-range light-helicity filters.

item.title: Rational Regulation of Ligand Conformation Toward Topology Reconfiguration for Sieving Butane Isomers
item.description:
A novel cage-like anion-pillared metal-organic framework SIFSIX-TEPH-Cu, constructed via ligand conformation-directed topology reconfiguration, exhibits outstanding molecular sieving performance for butane isomers.


ABSTRACT

Achieving one-step purification of n-C4H10 and iso-C4H10 from their isomeric mixtures with high efficiency and high purity is highly desirable yet extremely challenging, as it critically necessitates adsorbents that integrate size-exclusive sieving functionality, high n-C4H10 adsorption capacity, and fast adsorption kinetics. Herein, we synthesize a novel cage-like anion-pillared MOF adsorbent (SIFSIX-TEPH-Cu) through ligand-conformation-directed topology reconfiguration. Compared with the pillar-layer prototype SIFSIX-TEPE-Cu, SIFSIX-TEPH-Cu exhibits a distinctive “confined window–expanded cavity” synergistic pore structure, with pore apertures strategically situated between the kinetic diameters of n-C4H10 and iso-C4H10, thus enabling size-exclusive molecular sieving. Furthermore, the large cages and 3D pore architecture confer both a high n-C4H10 adsorption capacity (46.6 cm3/g) and a rapid adsorption rate (2.3 × 10−12 m2 s−1). Both kinetic analyses and DFT simulations provide mechanistic insights into the preferential adsorption and diffusion of n-C4H10. Dynamic breakthrough experiments demonstrate that SIFSIX-TEPH-Cu enables one-step purification of both n-C4H10 and iso-C4H10 from their binary mixture under various conditions, such as high temperatures, high gas flow rates, and high humidities. After one separation cycle, 23.8 L kg−1 high-purity iso-C4H10 (>99.99%) and 27.8 L kg−1 n-C4H10 (>99.0%) can be obtained, respectively.

item.title: Hydroxyl‐Orchestrated Crystallization and Affinity Sites in Covalent Organic Framework Membranes for One‐Step Selective Ternary Ion Separation
item.description:
Hydroxyl substitution simultaneously promotes crystallization and affinity-site formation in hydrazone-linked covalent organic framework membranes. By moderating framework assembly, reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding, and favoring keto-enamine tautomerization, hydroxyl groups generate ordered nanochannels and uranyl-binding pockets. Their combined effects enable preferential Cs+ permeation, Sr2+ exclusion, and affinity-mediated UO2 2+ retention within a single membrane.


ABSTRACT

One-step selective separation of multiple coexisting ions from complex aqueous media remains a formidable challenge. Here we report hydroxyl-orchestrated covalent organic framework (COF) membranes that couple framework crystallization with hydrazone-carbonyl pocket-site formation, enabling ternary separation of Cs+, Sr2+ and UO2 2+ in a single step. Hydroxyl substitution decelerates interfacial polymerization while reinforcing intralayer hydrogen bonding to stabilize ordered frameworks, yielding high crystallinity. Concurrently, hydroxyl-orchestrated enol-imine to keto-enamine tautomerization promotes the formation of hydrazone-carbonyl pocket sites for selective UO2 2+ chelation. The optimized membrane achieves a UO22+ uptake of 336 mg g−1 and a Cs+ permeation flux of 0.26 mol m−2 h−1, while exhibiting suppressed Sr2+ permeation. Under ternary conditions, Cs+/Sr2+ and Cs+/UO2 2+ separation factors reach 81.5 and 326.9, with stable performance over repeated cycles. These findings establish hydroxyl-orchestrated crystallization and pocket-site engineering as a powerful approach for multi-component ion separations.

item.title: Full‐Process Synergistic Optimization of Buried Interfaces via Molecule‐Assisted Co‐Assembly for Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
item.description:
Through a full-process synergistic optimization strategy, TFPPO suppresses SAM aggregation in solution, anchors onto the NiOx, and co-assembles with SAMs while optimizing their arrangement and strengthening their anchoring, thereby providing a favorable template for perovskite crystallization as well as regulating the chemical environment of the buried interface. A representative unencapsulated device retains around 97% of initial efficiency after more than 1800 h according to the ISOS-L-1 protocol.


ABSTRACT

Self-assembled monolayers (SAMs) are promising hole-selective contacts for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet insufficient substrate anchoring and weak buried-interface interactions limit device efficiency and stability. Here, we report a co-assembled SAM (Co-SAM) strategy that enables full-process synergistic optimization of the perovskite buried interface by introducing tris(4-fluorophenyl)phosphine oxide (TFPPO) into SAMs. TFPPO suppresses SAM aggregation in solution via its strongly polar P═O group and anchors onto NiOx, with its 4-fluorophenyl arms proposed to interact with unanchored hydroxyl groups of SAMs to strengthen anchoring and refine their arrangement. Furthermore, TFPPO optimizes the interfacial chemical states while serving as an effective template to direct high-quality perovskite crystal growth. Consequently, inverted PSCs based on the regulated SAMs achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 26.98% (stabilized PCE of 26.40%) and 20.65% for normal-bandgap (1.54 eV) and wide-bandgap (1.78 eV) devices, respectively. Moreover, a representative Co-SAM-modified device retains 97% of its initial efficiency after 1856 h of maximum power point tracking (ISOS-L-1), and Co-SAM-modified devices retain 92.36% of their initial efficiency after 2408 h of continuous aging at 65°C (ISOS-D-2).

item.title: Temporal Fidelity Reveals Transient Dissolution Chemistry at Dynamic Electrocatalyst Interfaces
item.description:
Transient dissolution can be more reliably interpreted when metal release remains temporally linked to the evolving electrochemical state. By suppressing transport-induced signal convolution, thin-layer electrochemical inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (EC-ICP-MS) restores this link, resolves overlapping dissolution events, and reveals weak redox- and reaction-coupled interfacial chemistry.


ABSTRACT

Dynamic electrocatalyst dissolution consists of short-lived, potential-dependent interfacial events tied to surface redox, reconstruction, and catalysis. Accurate interpretation of these processes requires preserving the temporal link between metal release and electrochemical state, but this link is often lost in electrochemical inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (EC-ICP-MS) due to transport-induced signal convolution. Here we reduce this distortion by using thin-layer hydrodynamic confinement to improve near-electrode convective removal. Paired-pulse dissolution experiments show that two consecutive 2 s dissolution inputs separated by 50 ms remain distinguishable. Cu-pulse residence-time-distribution measurements and computational fluid dynamics further identify electrode-region convective coverage and near-electrode flow velocity as key determinants of signal broadening. Applying this temporal fidelity to representative noble-metal, carbide, nitride, hydroxide, oxide, and single-atom interfaces under fast cyclic voltammetry reveals distinct dynamic dissolution fingerprints. This approach further resolves weak reoxidation-associated Ir dissolution from reduced IrOx and oxygen-reduction-associated suppression of spontaneous Cu release from Cu–N–C. These results highlight the importance of temporal fidelity for assigning transient dissolution chemistry at dynamic electrocatalyst interfaces.

item.title: Correction to “Iron/NHC‐Catalyzed Regio‐ and Stereoselective 1,6‐Additions of Aliphatic Grignard Reagents to α,β,γ,δ‐Unsaturated Carbonyl Compounds: Asymmetric Variants with Chiral NHCs”
item.description: Angewandte Chemie International Edition, EarlyView.

item.title: Conformational Locking in Covalent Organic Frameworks Promotes Coupled H2O2 Photosynthesis and Organic Valorization
item.description:
Conformational locking enhances framework planarity and prolongs the charge-separated-state lifetime in covalent organic frameworks, promoting photocatalytic H2O2 production coupled with selective benzylamine oxidation.


ABSTRACT

Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer a compelling platform for coupling photocatalytic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) production with organic valorization. However, the practical efficiency remains limited by rapid electron-hole recombination. Inspired by the conformational rigidity and planar geometry imposed by peptide bonds, we develop a conformational locking strategy that introduces a fused-ring linker, which restricts backbone rotation and thereby enhances framework planarity and conjugation, affording a series of COFs (TFPPy-DATMBP, TFPPy-DABP, and TFPPy-DAPy) with progressively improved planarity and conjugation. The conformationally locked TFPPy-DAPy achieves an impressive H2O2 production rate of 119.8 mmol g−1 h−1, with an apparent quantum yield up to 29.14% at 410 nm, while delivering a yield of >98% toward the high-value imine product. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that the conformationally locked TFPPy-DAPy extends the lifetime of the long-lived charge-separated state by approximately 10-fold to 102.87 ps, compared with 10.34 ps for TFPPy-DATMBP. This work establishes TFPPy-DAPy as an efficient photocatalyst for fine chemical co-production, and provides a generalizable molecular-level design strategy for developing advanced catalysts across diverse photocatalytic applications.

item.title: Band‐Filling Engineering in Covalent Organic Frameworks Through Host–Guest Charge‐Transfer Interactions
item.description:
Introduction of controlled amounts of the electron acceptor, 7,7,8,8-tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ), into the one-dimensional channels of tetrathiafulvalene-containing covalent organic framework (TTF-COF) enabled rational control over the charge states of the TTF moieties while preserving the framework structure. This band-filling control approach, with the aid of spectroscopic measurements and theoretical calculations, enabled the emergence of Pauli-like paramagnetism in the TCNQ-introduced TTF-COF hybrids.


ABSTRACT

Band-filling engineering is one of the most rational approaches to controlling the electronic properties of inorganic solids such as cuprates, in which electron/hole doping using heterovalent substitution leads to a rigid-band shift of the Fermi level. In organic solids, a significant obstacle to accurately predicting electronic properties is the difficulty in maintaining the packing structure during molecular substitution. Here, we utilized a covalent organic framework (COF) in which π-conjugated electron-donating molecules are covalently linked to form one-dimensional pore channels.
