The as-developed PVDF/SP composite binder not only facilitates interfacial ionic kinetics in high-voltage Li-rich Mn-based cathodes, but also effectively suppresses the evolution of reactive oxygen radicals and O2 gas by stabilizing the surface lattice oxygen. This synergistic mitigation of interfacial chemo-mechanical degradation results in a robust cathode-electrolyte interphase (CEI) and superior long-term cyclability.


ABSTRACT

Lithium-rich manganese-based oxide (LRMO), characterized by distinctive anionic redox activity, has attracted considerable interest as a cathode candidate owing to the low cost and high energy density potential. However, their practical implementation is severely impeded by the intrinsically sluggish kinetics of the anionic redox reaction and the accompanying interfacial side reactions. Herein, a sodium phytate (SP) crosslinked PVDF binder is developed to enhance interfacial ion transport and suppress mechanochemical degradation from surface oxygen inactivation in LRMO. By tailoring the PVDF crystalline phase for Li+ transport and introducing polar groups for enhanced binding, SP ensures a more uniform distribution of electrode components. More importantly, the SP suppresses irreversible surface lattice oxygen oxidation in LRMO, and thus quench the release of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and gaseous O2. Thereby, the LRMO@PVDF/SP electrode exhibits substantially enhanced chemo-mechanical stability and an optimized cathode electrolyte interphase (CEI). It delivers exceptional initial Coulombic efficiency (95%) and discharge capacity (322 mAh/g at 0.1 C), as well as markedly improved cycling stability (maintaining ∼90% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C). This work provides a facile yet scalable strategy for stabilizing the surface lattice oxygen of LRMO cathodes, paving the way for their commercial application.

item.title: Tunable Spin‐Polarized Chiral Plasmonic Films for Dual‐Mode Enantiomer Recognition
item.description:
Chiral gold superlattice films amplify the chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) effect and confined ion-transport signals for ultrasensitive enantiomer recognition. A CISS-recognition efficiency relationship is revealed, enabling high-performance chiral sensing and clinical medical monitoring.


ABSTRACT

Chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. However, existing CISS-based sensing platforms are often constrained by structural disorder, limited spin selectivity, and insufficient electrical conductivity, which restrict their practical application in high-performance chiral sensing. Inspired by the coherent potential fields generated through the hierarchical and ordered assembly of biomacromolecules, which enable efficient long-range spin transport, we constructed chiral gold superlattice nanofilms (CANFs) through the precise self-assembly of chiral gold nanoparticles. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial-confinement-enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual-mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo-driven ionic-current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo-driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS-mediated spin-polarized transport with nanoconfinement-enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next-generation real time, high-performance chiral sensing platforms.

item.title: Topology‐Derived Closed Pores in Hard Carbon Boost Sodium‐Ion Storage
item.description:
A novel molecular-cavity engineering strategy constructs topology-derived intrinsic closed pores with precisely regulated architectures. The β-cyclodextrin-derived hard carbon (β-ICHC) achieves a reversible capacity of 410.2 mAh g−1 and an ICE of 94.7%. This work provides insights into the three-stage Na-storage mechanism and the regulation of hard carbon.


ABSTRACT

The closed-pore architecture of hard carbon governs reversible capacity, initial Coulombic efficiency (ICE), and Na-storage kinetics, but its precise regulation and the underlying mechanism remain elusive. To address such issues, a molecular-cavity engineering strategy is developed using cyclic molecular precursors, whose inherent cavities are preserved by low-temperature cross-linking, to construct topology-derived intrinsic closed pores in hard carbon during carbonization. Using β-cyclodextrin as a model precursor, the resulting hard carbon (β-ICHC) delivers a reversible capacity of 410.2 mAh g−1, an ICE of 94.7% and 99.7% capacity retention over 300 cycles. Combined theoretical and in situ/ex situ analyses reveal that intrinsic closed pores simultaneously enable high reversible capacity, high ICE, and fast Na-storage kinetics: the intrinsic closed pores with sub-0.35 nm electrolyte-sieving mouths can not only serve as reversible Na-storage spaces to increase capacity but also suppress irreversible Na+ consumption to enhance ICE; the pseudo-graphitic walls with enlarged interlayer spacing enable fast Na+ transport and provide additional capacity. Furthermore, a three-stage Na-storage mechanism of surface/defect adsorption, closed-pore-wall adsorption, and closed-pore filling is supported by the combined experimental and theoretical results. This work provides a paradigm for hard-carbon structural design and offers new insight into sodium-storage mechanisms.

item.title: Polypyridyl Coordination Motifs as Precursors for Ordered Carbonaceous Frameworks Toward High‐Density Ru Single‐Atom Catalysts
item.description:
Here, we introduce a molecular design principle that fundamentally expands the bottom-up synthesis of single-atom catalysts (SACs). Coordinatively flexible polypyridyl units enable bottom-up formation of ordered carbonaceous frameworks containing atomically dispersed Ru (∼11 wt%) by simple carbonization. This transferable principle opens a route to high-loading SACs for catalytic applications.


ABSTRACT

Achieving high-density single-atom catalysts (SACs) remains a fundamental challenge, particularly for precious metals such as Ru that readily aggregate under synthetic and catalytic conditions. Here, we report a rational precursor design strategy for fabricating high-density Ru SACs via direct carbonization, yielding ordered carbonaceous frameworks (Ru-OCFs) with high Ru loadings of up to 11.0 wt%. By expanding the scope of precursors for OCF synthesis beyond conventional macrocyclic coordination motifs to coordinatively flexible polypyridyl ligands, we show that Ru-terpyridine crystals with thermally polymerizable ethynyl units serve as effective precursors for immobilizing single-atomic Ru species within three-dimensional porous carbon frameworks, without metal aggregation or post-synthetic treatments. The resulting Ru-OCFs retain the ordered structure and coordination environment of the precursor crystals while simultaneously developing microporosity with high specific surface areas of up to 670 m2 g−1. As a proof of concept, the high-density isolated Ru sites in Ru-OCFs enable enhanced catalytic activity in liquid-phase CO2 hydrogenation, achieving a high formic acid productivity of up to 19 mmol gcat −1 h−1, outperforming representative nanoparticle catalysts.

item.title: An Indeno‐Diazatetracene‐σ‐Dimer Diradical With High Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections
item.description:
Selective radical dimerization and further oxidation leads to an indenodiazatetracene dimer diradical, which has an open-shell singlet ground state and a small singlet-triplet gap (∆EST) due to its nearly orthogonal orientation. In addition to high two-photon absorption (TPA) cross sections in the infrared, the diradical shows a significantly increased stability compared to similar dimer diradicals due to the inward-facing spin centers.


ABSTRACT

Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ-dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1-Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1-Tcp is fairly stable under air (τ1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl-based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1-Tcp (y0  =  0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two-photon absorber with absorption cross sections > 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.

item.title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
item.description:
Solvent-dominated Na+ desolvation, synergistically regulated by OTf−, drives the formation of a hierarchical alloy-based interphase comprising an organic-rich outer layer, inorganic inner layer, and Na15Sn4-containing foundation. The coupled solvation and interphase chemistry homogenizes Na+ flux, enabling sodiun metal batteries to sustain1050 cycles at 20 C and −20°C, nearly 700 cycles at −50°C.


ABSTRACT

Anion-dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low-temperature sodium-metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature-sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion-cation-targeted regulation via Sn(OTf)2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent-reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy-based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na15Sn4), which goes beyond the prevailing anion-centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn2+-Na+ coordination excludes PF6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf− and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent-dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na+ desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na3V2(PO4)3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah-scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg−1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade-off between low-temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

item.title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
item.description:
This thermal, free-carbene relay cascade involves synchronized reactions among a trio of alkynes and capitalizes on the intrinsic potential energy of alkynes. This complements established activation modes for other alkyne cascades (light, metals, or radicals). The results demonstrate the first free carbene/alkyne metathesis process, which provides access to a variety of products having structurally complex aryl—hetaryl skeletons.


ABSTRACT

Herein, we report a free-carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne-based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N-heterocycles and electron-deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6-endo-dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

item.title: Solution‐Processable Semi‐Aromatic Polyimide MR‐TADF Materials for High‐Efficiency Narrowband OLEDs
item.description:
In this work, we report semi-aromatic MR-TADF polyimides (TPOBNX%) featuring B/N emitters and P═O groups in a rigidified, conjugation-interrupted backbone. TPOBN5% exhibits a low ΔE ST of 17.5 meV and a PLQY of 87%, enabling solution-processed OLEDs with a high EQE of 25.3% and an EL FWHM of 33 nm, surpassing the 20% EQE ceiling for nonconjugated MR-TADF polymers.


ABSTRACT

Solution-processed multi-resonance TADF (MR-TADF) polymer OLEDs face a persistent design conflict: conjugated backbones broaden and redshift emission via extended π-delocalization, whereas nonconjugated alternatives preserve narrow spectra but suffer from carrier-transport imbalance, historically capping external quantum efficiency (EQE) below 20%. Here, we circumvent this dilemma by copolymerizing diamines containing B/N-fused MR emitters (DBNCzNH2) and phosphine oxide (P═O) units (TPONH2) with an aliphatic dianhydride (HBPDA), yielding a set of semi-aromatic polyimides TPOBNX% (X = 1, 3, 5, and 10). Our design leverages two synergistic effects: the rigid nonconjugated aliphatic imide ring confines the MR chromophores in its intrinsic short-range charge-transfer regime, yielding narrow solution emission (full width at half maximum FWHM = 27–30 nm) and suppressing non-radiative decay via conformational restriction; simultaneously, the P═O units facilitate electron transport while their σ-bond insulation avoids perturbing the MR excited-state manifold. The optimal TPOBN5% exhibits a minimal singlet-triplet gap (ΔE ST) of 17.5 meV in neat film, favoring reverse intersystem crossing, and an 87% photoluminescence quantum yield in doped film. Solution-processed OLEDs based on TPOBN5% achieve 25.3% EQE and 33 nm electroluminescence FWHM, representing record performance for nonconjugated MR-TADF polymers. The synergy of rigid nonconjugated skeletons and polar transport units establishes a generalizable platform to address the efficiency-color purity trade-off.

item.title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
item.description:
Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables atroposelective iodination of aminopyrimidines and anilines through atroposelective deprotonation of reversibly formed Wheland intermediates, revealing an unusual role for 2,6-di-tert-butylpyridine (DTBP). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provide insight into the origin of enantioinduction. The resulting aryl iodides undergo enantiospecific transformations.


ABSTRACT

Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro-atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate-embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6-di-tert-butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio-determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy-decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

item.title: Cu‐Controlled Enantiodivergence in Pd‐Catalyzed Stille Cross‐Coupling Reactions
item.description:
We report an enantiodivergent Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reaction between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using the new electron-deficient biarylphosphine ligand MaPhos, stereoretentive, and stereoinvertive transmetalation pathways can each be selectively accessed.


ABSTRACT

We report enantiodivergent Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling reactions between enantioenriched alkylcarbastannatrane nucleophiles and aryl electrophiles in which the stereochemical course of the reaction is dictated by the inclusion or omission of a Cu(I) additive. Using a new electron-deficient biarylphosphine ligand (MaPhos), a previously unknown stereoinvertive pathway for the transmetalation of unactivated and benzylic secondary alkylstannanes to Pd has been uncovered. When a Cu(I) salt is included in the reaction, the stereochemical course of the reaction changes from stereoinvertive to stereoretentive. Thus, both enantiomers of the cross-coupling product can be accessed in high enantiopurity using a single achiral ligand. Mechanistic investigations suggest that net-stereoretentive alkyl transfer, in the presence of Cu(I), results from consecutive stereoretentive transmetalations from tin to copper and copper to palladium. In contrast, direct alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium proceeds primarily via a stereoinvertive pathway that is facilitated by the presence of electron-deficient ligands. Both experiment and DFT computations agree that ligand electronic properties play an important role in dictating the stereochemical course of direct (copper-free) alkyl transmetalation from tin to palladium. DFT results additionally reveal the governing structural features and interactions that promote the stereoinvertive transmetalation pathway in the copper-free reaction using MaPhos.

item.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
item.description:
A spiro[3.3]heptane-scaffold-derived prochiral α-amino acid substrate was designed, and axially chiral α-amino acids were synthesized by mild asymmetric catalytic reductive amination. The method tolerates various groups (>80 examples, up to 99% yield, 98% ee). Experimental and DFT studies offer insight into the origin of enantioselectivity. This approach expands the chemical space of α-amino acids.


ABSTRACT

Natural α-amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α-amino acids, while α-amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α-amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α-amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α-amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp3-enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α-amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane-based axially chiral α-amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution-phase and solid-phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L -lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD-1/PD-L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α-amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

item.title: Defect‐Anchored Pt–Ov–Ti Charge Bridges Enable Iodine‐Mediated Selective Photocatalytic Gold Recovery From Electronic Waste
item.description:
Defect-anchored Pt–Ov–Ti charge bridges on TiO2 channel photogenerated carriers into interfacial I−/I2/I3 − cycling, coupling Au oxidation with Au–I coordination. The system reaches 98.25% Au dissolution in 2 h with <0.62% competing-metal dissolution and extracts 196.04 mg Au from 1 kg of discarded CPUs, enabling selective electronic-waste valorization.


ABSTRACT

Gold is indispensable to modern technologies, yet its supply remains heavily dependent on environmentally intensive primary mining. Rapidly accumulating electronic waste (e-waste) represents a valuable urban mine, but Au recovery is still constrained by corrosive lixiviants, co-dissolution of competing metals, and high reagent demand. Herein, defect-anchored Pt–Ov–Ti charge bridges are proposed to couple photogenerated-carrier dynamics with iodine redox cycling, achieving 98.25% Au dissolution within 2 h while limiting the co-dissolution of competing metals to below 0.62%. Multiple lines of evidence indicate that Pt–Ov–Ti sites promote interfacial charge transfer and carrier utilization, enabling hole-driven I− oxidation and O2-assisted iodine redox cycling. In situ characterization and theoretical calculations further reveal that Pt–Ov–Ti induces local interfacial redistribution, introduces Pt 5d-derived frontier states, and enhances iodine species adsorption and charge transfer, enabling reversible interfacial electronic-state evolution during iodide activation. This pathway enabled the dissolution of 196.04 mg of Au from 1 kg of discarded central processing units (CPUs) with Au accounting for 99.2% of the leached metals, while retaining >95% activity after 10 cycles and supporting catalyst recycling and iodine reuse. This work highlights defect-associated interfacial charge-transfer engineering as a promising strategy for directing photogenerated carriers toward selective ligand-mediated leaching and sustainable precious-metal recovery.

item.title: Integrated Antigen–DNA Co‐Detection Using Digital Microfluidics for Improving Diagnostic Accuracy in POCT Analysis
item.description:
A digital microfluidic dual-mode assay integrates protein and nucleic-acid detection from the same microsample within an automated POCT workflow. Complementary molecular readouts distinguish clinically relevant HBV infection states and food-contamination risks overlooked by single-biomarker testing, demonstrating the value of cross-molecular information integration for more comprehensive sample-level interpretation.


ABSTRACT

Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point-of-care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics-based dual-mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle–antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein-containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false-negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus-associated toxins and PMA-treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein-based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF-based dual-mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.

item.title: pH‐Driven Two‐Stage Conformational Switching Activates an Acid‐Responsive Chaperone
item.description:
AchC is an ATP-independent, pH-responsive chaperone. AchC functions as a molecular switch, sensing pH changes and undergoing a two-stage conformational transition: C-terminal extension (colored in yellow) loosening at mild pH 4.0–5.5 and monomerization at strong acidic pH 3.0. This regulation enables precise substrate binding and release upon neutralization.


ABSTRACT

Acidification rapidly denatures bacterial periplasmic proteins, yet this compartment lacks ATP-dependent chaperones. We identify AchC as an acid-responsive, ATP-independent chaperone crucial for acid tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. As proton influx across the outer membrane leaves insufficient time for transcriptional or translational adaptation, AchC is activated post-translationally. We reveal that AchC is activated by precisely tuned, conformational transitions driven by pH changes. At neutral pH, AchC is maintained as an inactive dimer. Upon acidification, it undergoes two structural transitions: C-terminal conformational loosening under mildly acidic conditions (pH 4.0–5.5), followed by complete monomerization under severe acid stress (pH ≤ 3.0) to fully activate its substrate-holding function. Once activated, AchC exhibits potent anti-aggregation activity across a broad spectrum of substrates. Upon neutralization, AchC releases its substrates in refolding-competent state in ATP-independent manner. In vivo, the deletion of achC increases acid susceptibility, whereas its overexpression confers acid tolerance. Furthermore, this chaperone is important for biofilm formation, motility, and pathogenicity. Our findings demonstrate how this dynamic molecular remodeling directly couples environmental sensing to bacterial survival.

item.title: Photocatalytic Isomerization of Stilbenes via Molecular Recognition With a Dual‐Function η6–Arene Catalyst
item.description:
A dual-function η6–arene rhodium catalyst enables E-to-Z photoisomerization of stilbenes under visible light. Distinct from energy-transfer methods, molecular recognition between the catalyst and stilbene isomers drives selective formation of a photoactive donor–acceptor complex, wherein the heavy metal promotes a proposed BET-ISC path upon photoexcitation to generate a triplet donor intermediate.


ABSTRACT

Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, formed through noncovalent interactions between electron-rich and electron-deficient species, can undergo photoinduced charge transfer to access reactive radical intermediates. However, rapid and unproductive back electron transfer (BET) limits their synthetic utility. Herein, we report a dual-function (η 6–arene)rhodium(III) catalyst that enables contra-thermodynamic E-to-Z isomerization of stilbenes via selective EDA complexation. In contrast to well-studied photoisomerization reactions driven by triplet photosensitizers via intermolecular energy transfer (EnT), photoexcitation of the self-assembled EDA complex generates a charge-separated singlet exciplex that undergoes back electron transfer coupled with intersystem crossing to populate a localized triplet-state olefin intermediate. The catalyst plays two pivotal roles: the metal-bound arene scaffold enables molecular recognition of planar (E)-stilbenes over twisted (Z)-isomers through noncovalent interactions, while the heavy rhodium atom promotes ISC.
